etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English probable, from Old French probable, from Latin probābilis (“that may be proved, credible”), from probāre (“to test, examine”); see probe, probity, prove. Compare recent doublet provable.

definitions.definition: Likely or most likely to be true.
Supporting, or giving ground for, belief, but not demonstrating.

quote.text: From an examination of the Teutonic words for "temple" Grimm has made it probable that amongst the Germans the oldest sanctuaries were natural woods.
